speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and did you experience any recent injury or trauma to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear or feel a "pop" at the moment of injury, and are you able to fully straighten or bend the tip of the finger? I also need to know if you experienced any immediate numbness or tingling in the digit.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a visible retraction of the tip of the finger, making it look like a "jersey finger," and does the pain worsen when you try to actively flex the tip against resistance? I would like to confirm if the finger stays extended while the others curl into a fist. REQUEST TEST: X-ray of the right hand and finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: The mechanism of injury and your inability to flex the fingertip are classic signs of a flexor tendon avulsion. Given the negative X-ray, I suspect the tendon pulled off without taking a bone fragment with it. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus avulsion)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
